title: Syntomicity from a finite principal cover by relative complete intersections
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $m\geq0$ be an integer, and let $g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_m\in D$ satisfy $\sum_{a=1}^m h_ag_a=1$. For $g\in D$ write $D_g=D[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Suppose each composite $A\to D\to D_{g_a}$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]: there is an $A$-algebra presentation $D_{g_a}\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_a}]/(f_{a,1},\ldots,f_{a,c_a})$ whose nonzero residue-field fibres all have dimension $n_a-c_a$. Then $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $D\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. The empty cover is allowed: its displayed relation forces $D=0$.

source.place: Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic), with relative global complete intersection charts syntomic by Tag 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection).

proof.text: If $D=0$, it is finitely presented over $A$ by $A/(1)$, its underlying module is zero and hence flat (tensoring any injection with it gives $0\to0$), and every fibre is zero, a global and therefore local complete intersection by the zero-ring convention (use the one-element cover indexed by $1=0$). This proves the conclusion in this case. In particular it handles $m=0$, since the given relation then reads $0=1$. Henceforth assume $D\ne0$, so $m>0$.

For each $a$, choose the presentation $T_a=A[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_a}]/(f_{a,1},\ldots,f_{a,c_a})\cong D_{g_a}$ in the hypothesis. It is a finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat] with these exact equations and their assumed fibre-dimension condition; it gives flatness of $A\to T_a$. The displayed $A$-algebra isomorphism identifies its underlying $A$-module with $D_{g_a}$, so the tensor-injectivity definition of flatness gives flatness of $A\to D_{g_a}$ as well.

source.place: Tag 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection), proof: finite presentation from the presentation and flatness from 00SV.

proof.text: Put $s=\{g_a:1\le a\le m\}\subseteq D$. The relation $\sum h_ag_a=1$ shows it generates the unit ideal: multiplying this equality by $d\in D$ writes $d=\sum(dh_a)g_a$. Step 2 supplies flatness and finite presentation of every composite $A\to D_g$ for $g\in s$, even if indices repeat. Apply [lem-trf-flat-ring-map-principal-cover] and [lem-trf-finite-presentation-ring-map-principal-cover] with the ring map $\varphi$ and this set $s$. Thus $A\to D$ is flat and of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic), applying Tags 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), part (5), and 00EP (lemma-cover-upstairs), part (2).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=D\otimes_A k$, and write $\bar g_a=g_a\otimes1$. Base change the chosen presentation of $T_a$ along $A\to k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change]. It gives $T_a\otimes_A k\cong k[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_a}]/(\bar f_{a,1},\ldots,\bar f_{a,c_a})$, a relative global complete intersection over $k$. Its only residue-field fibre is itself, so when nonzero its dimension is $n_a-c_a$; when zero use the convention in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. In both cases it is a global complete intersection. To identify this ring with $F_{\bar g_a}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] to $D\to D_{g_a}$ and $D\to F$. The elementary tensor reassociation $F\otimes_D D_{g_a}\cong D_{g_a}\otimes_A k$ sends $(d\otimes\lambda)\otimes z$ to $dz\otimes\lambda$, with inverse $z\otimes\lambda\mapsto(1\otimes\lambda)\otimes z$. Combining these identifications gives $F_{\bar g_a}\cong D_{g_a}\otimes_A k$, whose inverse sends $(d/g_a^r)\otimes\lambda$ to $(d\otimes\lambda)/\bar g_a^r$. The balanced relations check these formulas on pure tensors. Consequently every $F_{\bar g_a}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Tag 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic), fibre locality, expanded using Tags 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection), 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 00S9 (definition-lci-field).

proof.text: The finite presentation of $D$ in step 3 provides finitely many $A$-algebra generators $d_1,\ldots,d_N$. Their images $d_i\otimes1$ generate $F$ as a $k$-algebra: each pure tensor $d\otimes\lambda$ is $\lambda$ times the polynomial expression for $d$ after applying $A\to k$, and tensors are sums of pure tensors. The given relation maps to $\sum(h_a\otimes1)\bar g_a=1$ in $F$. For any prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $F$, not all the $\bar g_a$ can belong to $\mathfrak q$, since otherwise $1\in\mathfrak q$. Hence the principal opens $D(\bar g_a)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Together with step 4 this is exactly the defining cover by global complete intersections in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Thus $F$ is a local complete intersection, including $F=0$, and $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00SO (lemma-local-syntomic) and 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection); the fibre-locality sentence is expanded with base change and explicit tensor/fraction formulas.
